title: Factory and Abstract Factory
idea: A Factory pattern puts object creation behind one method, so callers ask for a kind and get a ready object. Abstract Factory creates whole families of matching objects.

analogy.text: A coffee counter. You ask for a flat white; the barista picks the beans, milk and cup. A franchise kit ships every matching cup and lid together.
analogy.breaks: A barista improvises; a factory only builds kinds it knows.

points: Callers depend on what an object does, never on its concrete class.
A simple factory maps kinds to classes, keeping `new` in one place.
Gang of Four Factory Method: subclasses override one `create` method to pick the product.
Abstract Factory swaps a whole family at once, so parts never mismatch.

steps.caption: The caller asks for a notifier by kind. It never names a concrete class.
`create` receives the kind. Every construction decision lives here, in one place.
The factory looks the kind up in its private registry map.
The map returns `SmsNotifier`, and the factory runs `new` on it.
The object travels back and the caller calls `send('ada')`. It only knows the method exists.
An unknown kind such as `'fax'` fails fast with a clear error, not a silent `undefined`.

code.title: Simple factory with a registry
code.caption: Add a `PushNotifier` class, register it as `'push'`, and create one. `create` never changes.

walk.text: Two products share one shape: a `send(to)` method.
The registry maps each kind to its class.
`register` adds kinds from outside, so the factory stays closed for edits.
`create` looks up, validates, then builds. It is the only `new` callers need.
Callers pass a string and get an object, or a clear error.

code.title: Abstract Factory: families
code.caption: Each kit builds a matching charger and refunder. `settle` cannot mix a fake charger with a live refunder.

walk.text: Two families of products: live and fake, each with a charger and a refunder.
Each kit is a factory with one method per product in the family.
`settle` takes a kit, so tests pass `FakePayments` and production passes `LivePayments`.

pitfalls: Skip the factory when only one class exists and none is planned; `new` is fine.
Avoid a `switch` on kind inside `create`; a registry map stays open for extension.
Throw on an unknown kind instead of returning `null` or a silent default.

quiz.why: `makers['z']` is `undefined`, so `??` falls back to `A`. That silent default is exactly what hides typos in real factories.

takeaway: Ask a factory for a kind; let one place decide which class to build.
